A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAM2Act, SAM2Act+, and MemoryBench. All 18 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison through readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLBench, Colosseum, MemoryBench, and real-robot experiments in Tables 1–4, plus encoder and upsampling ablations in Table 7.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results, reports retrained MemoryBench outcomes, and adds original encoder ablations and detailed Colosseum results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The SAM2-based coarse-to-fine architecture, multi-resolution upsampling, memory components, freezing strategy, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix A newly documents module internals rather than establishing an architectural revision. The changed memory-window length is an experimental configuration change.

E1.justification: Identified coverage remains 18 RLBench tasks, 20 Colosseum tasks with 13 perturbation categories, three MemoryBench tasks, and four real-robot tasks. The drawer waypoint revision preserves the task requirements and environment. The added result tables describe retained coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's PerAct, RVT, RVT-2, and SAM-E comparisons, v3 Table 7 adds Image-BC CNN/ViT, C2F-ARM-BC, HiveFormer, PolarNet, Act3D, 3D Diffuser Actor, 3D-LOTUS, and ARP+. Table 9 also adds DINOv2 and Depth Anything V2 encoder comparators. These substantially broaden the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix H explicitly reports adding a closing waypoint to reopen_drawer demonstrations, retraining all policies on that updated task, and increasing SAM2Act+'s memory window from 8 to 10. These are limited changes within retained coverage. Table 6 still lists the old window and associated settings, leaving the documentation inconsistent.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix E.1 adds DINOv2 and Depth Anything V2 substitutions to test whether the encoder advantage extends beyond comparison with SAM. The existing upsampling ablations and Colosseum robustness comparisons remain. The new Colosseum table provides detailed scores for the existing evaluation rather than a new robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions retain four evaluations for RLBench/MemoryBench and three for Colosseum. However, v3 Table 3's aggregate deviations match dispersion across task means, whereas v1's SAM2Act and SAM2Act+ deviations match averages of per-task deviations. Neither explains the aggregation rule, so a changed estimator cannot be reliably distinguished from inconsistent numerical reporting.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces reopen_drawer success rates of 44%, 44%, and 75% with 60%, 48%, and 84% for RVT-2, SAM2Act, and SAM2Act+, respectively, under revised conditions. SAM2Act+'s aggregate becomes 94.3% instead of 91.3%. v3 also adds extensive baseline and Colosseum results, plus encoder-ablation averages of 82.2% for DINOv2 and 81.1% for Depth Anything V2. Existing Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain their scores.

T1.justification: The Markov-condition equation in Section 3.1 and the multi-resolution upsampling equations in Section 4.1 are unchanged. No new propositions, proofs, formal assumptions, or derivations appear in the expanded appendices.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain the same. The introduction updates the MemoryBench achievement from 91.3% success and a 37.6-point margin to 94.3% and 39.3 points; the abstract now explicitly reports 94.3%. The conclusion drops the assertion of reduced uncertainty. The RLBench and generalization headline claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a substantive limitation: the memory architecture appears unable to retain semantic attributes such as color, despite retaining spatial information. Appendix H identifies drawer-handle collisions and explains the waypoint correction. Existing limitations concerning dexterous continuous control and fixed memory windows remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix A supplies substantial previously missing implementation information: CLIP tokenization, attention-layer counts, positional embeddings, memory-encoder operations, and feature dimensions of 128 and 64. v3 also identifies the real-robot software stack and documents the benchmark update. Reproducibility remains limited by Table 6 retaining settings inconsistent with Appendix H.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds prior work on the ArmarX cognitive memory architecture. Additional citations support the implementation, alternative encoders, and broader comparisons, including positioning against ARP+. The principal relationship to RVT-2, SAM2, and SAM-E and most related-work discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language and terminology edits, improves appendix cross-references, and reorganizes numbered supplementary sections into Appendices A–I with additional subsections. The introduction, method narrative, training description, and existing task descriptions remain largely intact.

P2.justification: New Tables 7 and 8 substantially expand the displays with a broader RLBench comparison matrix and task-by-perturbation Colosseum results; the ablation table also gains rows. Figure 2 corrects and expands MemoryBench instruction annotations, including the previously incorrect rearrange-block description. Existing architecture and robot-setup figures are retained but relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability and reproducibility through detailed memory-module documentation, stronger comparator coverage, additional encoder controls, and task-level Colosseum results. It also addresses a documented drawer-collision problem and acknowledges a semantic-memory limitation. These gains are tempered by conflicting memory-window settings, Table 3's outdated 37.6-point caption, and unexplained aggregate uncertainty calculations. The higher MemoryBench scores alone do not establish improvement because the experimental conditions changed.
